summary: The blanket PR-171 no-go is false on its stated Gamma >= 0 domain and underdetermined away from that boundary. A narrower near-FLRW, first-order, source-free drag stability lemma is defensible, but it is not a shear-leakage ceiling or isotropy theorem.

findings.statement: The stated domain includes Gamma=0. Hervik and Lim's full tilted Bianchi VIII gamma-law solutions generically approach extreme tilt for 1 < gamma < 2. Choosing gamma=5/4 gives w=1/4 < 1/3 with rho>0, p=rho/4, c_s^2=1/4, positive enthalpy, causal sound speed, and the null/dominant energy conditions, while |v| tends to 1. This is a physically admissible persistent-tilt falsifier at an allowed boundary and retires the universal no-go. Coley-Hervik-Lim also explicitly show that late-time tilt behavior below the radiation value is Bianchi-class dependent, so their work cannot be cited as a generic decay theorem. For Gamma>0, Q^mu proportional to relative velocity does not specify the force projector, normalization, energy-transfer component, equation-of-state closure, sound speed, frame, or Bianchi geometry, so the remaining assertion is underdetermined rather than proved.

findings.required_disposition: Do not freeze a conclusion number or advertise a generic fluid no-go. Record the Gamma=0 Bianchi VIII fixture as a preregistered kill test. Any strict Gamma>0 claim must be a separately specified domain with a complete covariant interaction and geometry closure; it cannot exclude this falsifier post hoc.

findings.statement: A defensible surrogate uses N=ln a, an expanding near-FLRW normal frame n^a, dust c plus a constant barotropic X fluid with h_X=(1+w_X)rho_X>0, a=1-3w_X>0, aligned nonrelativistic tilts, no persistent forcing, and a pure linear momentum force f_X=-D(v_X-v_c), f_c=-f_X with D>=0. The 4-state equations are rho_X'=-3(1+w_X)rho_X, rho_c'=-3rho_c, v_X'=-(1-3w_X)v_X-x(v_X-v_c), v_c'=-v_c+y(v_X-v_c), where x=D/(H h_X)>=0, y=D/(H rho_c)>=0, and h_X x=rho_c y. Equivalently r'= -3w_X r with r=rho_X/rho_c gives a 3-state system. The frozen velocity matrix A=[[-a-x,x],[y,-1-y]] has tr A=-(a+x+y+1)<0, det A=a(1+y)+x>0, and characteristic polynomial lambda^2+(a+x+y+1)lambda+a(1+y)+x, so both eigenvalues are negative. In fact its infinity-norm logarithmic measure is max(-a,-1), giving uniform contraction if a(N) is bounded positive and x,y remain nonnegative. For a general barotrope the threshold is c_a^2=dp/d rho<1/3, not merely w<1/3. This result is conditional on the specified frame/closure; exact RW use also requires h_X v_X+rho_c v_c=0. A 2x2 first-order velocity system cannot establish shear leakage: tilted-perfect-fluid anisotropic stress is pi_ab=sum_i h_i v_{i<a}v_{i b>}+O(v^4), hence quadratic around zero tilt. A Bianchi-I-like fourth variable would obey Sigma'=-(3+H'/H)Sigma+(8 pi G/H^2)pi_parallel only after geometry, normalization, Einstein constraints, H(N), and curvature terms are frozen. The preregistered unforced suppression functional may be S_v=||[1,-1]Phi(N_f,N_i)||, while a zero-initial-state forced anisotropic-stress functional must be quadratic, G_u_to_Pi^(2)=sup_{u!=0} ||Pi[z(u)]||_infinity/||u||_2^2. Pi/source is amplitude- and dimension-dependent and is not a linear gain. Freeze interval, norm, source, initial data, coupling history, background, frame, geometry, and admissibility before evaluation; freeze no numerical conclusion.

findings.safe_claim: Within the frozen near-FLRW two-fluid drag model, positive-enthalpy constant-barotropic X with c_a^2=w_X<1/3 and nonnegative momentum-conserving drag has a locally linearly stable comoving fixed point. This C2 hypothesis-only statement is not an isotropy proof, a generic no-go, a persistent-shear bound, or a Bianchi-family claim.
required_tests: Symbolically verify trace, determinant, characteristic polynomial, momentum-conservation identity, and the c_a^2 generalization.
Numerically integrate time-varying admissible x(N), y(N) cases and compare against the infinity-norm contraction bound.
Run the preregistered gamma=5/4 Bianchi VIII, Gamma=0 kill fixture; any persistent or extreme tilt returns FAIL.
Test a separately specified strict-positive-drag covariant model only after its projector, Q^0, EOS/sound speed, geometry, constraints, source space, and norms are frozen.
Treat missing required CAS axes as CAS_BLOCKED; do not convert this hand derivation into a four-axis pass.

assumptions: Metric signature (-,+,+,+); c=1; 8 pi G is retained in the schematic shear equation.
n^a is the homogeneous normal/geometric congruence and u_i^a=n^a+v_i^a+O(v_i^2); frame labels are not interchangeable.
The stability lemma is first order in aligned tilt about v_X=v_c=0, with H>0, rho_i>0, h_X>0, D>=0, and no external persistent source.
The drag law is a stipulated closure, not derived from the phrase Q^mu proportional to relative velocity.
Shear and anisotropic-stress statements require at least second order in tilt and a named Bianchi geometry.
